newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO AND RAUL BOTH FIT FOR CUP CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO AND RAUL BOTH FIT FOR CUP CLASH.

text.p: Barcelona striker Ronaldo and his Real Madrid counterpart Raul Gonzalez have both recovered from injuries and are ready for Thursday's fourth round Spanish Cup tie.

Both men are conscious that victory could prove a major psychological blow in the race for the league title, especially for leaders Real, who must meet Real Betis and Deportivo Coruna, third and fourth respectively, within a two-week period.
The last confrontation between the two ended in victory for Real, who took the league match in the Santiago Bernabeu stadium 2-0.
For Ronaldo the match proved a disaster.

The young Brazilian was marked out of the game by Real central defenders Rafael Alkorta and Fernando Hierro, and failed to connect to a straightforward header which would have put his side back in the game.
Since then the rise of Raul has proved irresistible.

The 19-year old capped a superb performance in the game at Atletico with a magnificent individual goal, leading Spanish commentators to make him the standard-bearer of home-grown talent against what they call 'the invasion' of foreign players, led by Ronaldo.
Fans surveyed in polls comparing the two came out in favour of the Spaniard.
But understandably supporters are anxious to see pair two together again, leading to a new outburst of media attention ahead of what one columnist has dubbed ''this week's game of the century'''.
''I hope we win with a late goal, so they suffer a bit," said Real president Lorenzo Sanz, in reply to a comment by Barcelona vice-president Joan Gaspart, who said he hoped his side won 12-0.
Barcelona got half way to that total with the help of a Ronaldo hat-trick in Sunday's emphatic league win over Rayo Vallecano.
Even so fans at the Camp Nou were quick to whistle at their side for not working hard enough with the score at 5-0, leading manager Bobby Robson to issue a plea for unity.
"I believe that within a club there can never be two teams," said Robson, in an open letter to supporters published on Wednesday in the sport daily 'Marca'.
"I would ask for your patience....at times I feel the same way...sometimes I don't like the team either." continued Robson "We want to be the first to beat Real Madrid this season."
Despite the importance of the clash Robson's opposite number is considering resting players for the game.
"On Sunday we have an important game with Deportivo," said Fabio Capello, who has seen Raul recover from a knock picked up in last week's home victory over Celta Vigo.
"I have my doubts, I'm thinking about it," said Capello when asked who he would leave out.
But Capello is in no doubt that Robson's principal weapon lies in another player who has shaken off an injury ahead of Thursday's game.
"(Ronaldo) is dangerous and he has talent," he conceded.
